answer: In an agent economy serving a wharf, every trading identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can rent a lantern or book cargo across a bridge. Creating more names does not bypass the bond: operating 1,000 identities requires $100,000 locked at once. This makes a sybil swarm costly in scarce capital and foregone interest, while the lock prevents an attacker from recycling one bond rapidly through fresh identities.
